tagline: A city-state with hot nights, dense towers and an early national heat stress advisory.

hap.text: Singapore launched a national Heat Stress Advisory in July 2023. It rates heat stress as low, moderate or high from the wet-bulb globe temperature, and tells people what to do at each level. Since March 2025 a heatwave is declared when the daily maximum reaches at least 35 °C and the daily mean at least 29 °C for three days in a row; a taskforce of 37 public agencies then opens air-conditioned cooling spaces in community centres. In March 2026 a Heat Resilience Policy Office was set up to coordinate action across agencies, oversee research and draft a heat resilience action plan.

tagline: A tropical megacity where heat costs lives, livelihoods and a share of the city’s economy.

hap.text: For the 2026 hot season Bangkok opened 304 cooling centres in schools, health centres and district offices. The city’s own Urban Heat Management Action Plan for 2026 has 22 indicators and a committee chaired by a deputy governor; its targets include cooling rooms in 80% of schools and public health service centres, at least two cooling points in every district, and home visits to at least 5,000 vulnerable households a year during heat alerts. A 2026 financing strategy with UNDP costs the plan at about THB 146 million to set up and THB 10.8 million a year to run, mostly from existing city budgets, and notes that running costs are not always covered.
